content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am attempting to transmit input from sensors to the [product_name] using Ethernet, as the sensors are too distant for wired connections. My only viable option is to use a TP-Link device for this purpose. The sensors are connected to one side of an IoT device and, on the other side, to my [product_name] via an Ethernet cable. My question is: when the signals reach the [product_name], how are they organized, and which variables do they use? Is there any menu within the [product_name] where this can be set? Thank you,

No. The [product_name] communicates over Ethernet TCP/IP using either the S7 protocol or Modbus TCP/IP. It's unlikely that the sensors support the S7 protocol. Therefore, only Modbus TCP/IP could work, but not every [product_name] supports Modbus TCP/IP—only models from [version_no] or newer.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing methods to connect remote sensors to a [product_name] via Ethernet when direct wiring is impractical. The main limitation is the supported protocols, as the [product_name] uses either S7 protocol or Modbus TCP/IP, and only certain versions support Modbus TCP/IP. This leads to difficulties in integrating IoT-based sensors with the [product_name] system due to protocol constraints.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] to automatically recognize and allocate incoming sensor data received through Ethernet to appropriate variables or menu settings, enabling straightforward integration and configuration.
